desk_read: Yesterday's dominant theme was aggressive macro de-risking as energy markets suffered severe selling alongside equities. WTI Crude Oil and Brent (NYMEX) plunged -7.36% and -7.63% respectively, driven by massive surges in net open interest of +171.7k contracts and +23.1k contracts as new shorts flooded the market under backwardated curves. Equity indices mirrored this defensive posture, with Nasdaq 100 open interest jumping +10.6% on a -1.42% price drop and S&P 500 adding +32.1k contracts of new short positioning. Meanwhile, Gold managed a +1.81% price gain despite falling open interest of -5.7k contracts, reflecting short covering rather than fresh commitment.
oil_read: Yesterday's session saw WTI (CLZ26) fall -7.36% with total open interest surging +171.7k contracts (+15.2%) on volume 1.0x its 20-day average, signaling new shorts and backwardation with the CLZ26-CLK27 spread at +8.94 $/bbl. Brent (BZF27) dropped -7.63% as total open interest rose +23.1k contracts (+18.0%) on volume 1.0x its 20-day average, also indicating new shorts and backwardation with the BZZ26-BZK27 spread at +22.49 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil shows a mildly bearish bias driven by new shorts and a weakening backwardation curve, while Brent remains neutral on new shorts with a steepening backwardation, suggesting persistent downward pressure rather than an immediate reversal. S&P 500 displays a mildly bearish bias with volume at 1.5x the 20-day average, where the fresh positioning supports the continuation of the current downside move. Silver registers a mildly bullish bias with new longs on volume at 1.6x the 20-day average, meaning this high-conviction buying supports the upward move. Overall, the cross-market flow reveals diverging sentiment with high-volume participation in equities and metals, pointing to selective short-term directional conviction.
